title: Lesson 40 adjectival NNC function and modification review

groups.title: Adjectival function and the absolutive boundary
groups.proposal: Treat adjectival as a syntactic function of an already typed NNC or VNC Result, preserve the ordinary absolutive boundary, and keep English adjective translation non-authorizing.
groups.readingJob: Show the exact Source unit, its own morphology, the adjectival relation, and the translation boundary.
groups.decisionSplit: The Source owner settles morphology; the user chooses only a genuine modification relation or clause arrangement.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create an adjective stem class, infer grammar from translation, or rebuild a Source from a displayed string.

groups.title: Exceptional adjectival NNC families
groups.proposal: Preserve huēi, nepāpan, cēl, and el through their own exact pronominal, affinity, number, and possessor-included owners before they enter adjectival modification.
groups.readingJob: Show the exceptional Source family, number or possessor facts, exact NNC Result, and adjectival use.
groups.decisionSplit: Only an ambiguity licensed by the exceptional Source owner is selectable; inherited facts remain automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not generalize exceptional forms into a productive adjective class or use example identity as route authority.

groups.title: Patientive and potential-patient adjectival function
groups.proposal: Continue from an exact owner-issued patientive or potential-patient NNC Result and preserve its resultant-state analysis inside adjectival modification.
groups.readingJob: Show the patientive Source history, patientive kind, resultant-state relation, and modifying clause.
groups.decisionSplit: The derivational owner settles the patientive form; the user chooses only a genuinely open relation or arrangement.
groups.controlPolicy: Never continue from a patientive-looking nounstem string, formula, translation, or copied Result.

groups.title: Nominalized VNC and customary adjectival function
groups.proposal: Continue from exact nominalized VNC Results, including customary agentive and patientive formations, without collapsing their Source operations into adjectival modification.
groups.readingJob: Show the VNC Source, nominalization, agentive or patientive identity, and adjectival relation.
groups.decisionSplit: Nominalization is settled upstream; only a genuine clause relation or arrangement remains selectable.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer agentive or patientive identity from a visible ending or English adjective.

groups.title: Preterit-agentive adjectival function
groups.proposal: Continue from exact preterit-agentive Results across verb classes, compounds, transitivity, denominal sources, and ownerhood formations while retaining all upstream identity.
groups.readingJob: Show the exact VNC history, class-conditioned agentive Result, compound or ownerhood structure, and adjectival use.
groups.decisionSplit: Upstream owners settle class and formation; the user chooses only a genuinely open modification relation.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not reconstruct the agentive from surface spelling or limit productive continuation to Canvas examples.

groups.title: Root-plus-ya adjectival formations
groups.proposal: Preserve the obsolete root-plus-ya and denominal-ti-ya formation as a typed Source history, including its stated exceptions, before adjectival use.
groups.readingJob: Show the root or denominal Source, ya formation, exception status, and adjectival Result.
groups.decisionSplit: A Source-history choice appears only where the typed evidence genuinely leaves alternatives open.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not derive root-plus-ya from a matching surface string or make its obsolete examples a whitelist.

groups.title: Synonymous adjectival formation systems
groups.proposal: Keep ni, hui, hua, ihui, ahui, ti-ya, c-ti-ya, and z-ti-ya histories distinct even where their adjectival Results are synonymous.
groups.readingJob: Show each typed Source history, shared reading, retained contrast, and exact modifying Result.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a Source analysis only under genuine contextual ambiguity; synonymy does not merge owners.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not select Source history from English meaning, visible spelling, or example frequency.

groups.title: Predicate-adjective sentences and multiple nuclei
groups.proposal: Use ordinary owner-issued NNC sentence Results for single predicate adjectives and the canonical adjectival-modification owner for multiple-nucleus structures.
groups.readingJob: Show each nuclear clause, shared referent, modification relation, order, marking, and complete sentence Result.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only genuine topology, order, adjunctor, or contact relations exposed by the canonical owner.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not flatten multiple nuclei into modifier-word plus head-word strings or infer structure from translation.
